June 9, 1983) is an American [[basketball]] coach and former professional player who is an assistant coach for the [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's Hawks]] of the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]]. ==Early life== Jones was born in [[Morgantown, West Virginia]] and raised in [[Chester, Pennsylvania]]. Jones graduated from the American Christian School of [[Aston, Pennsylvania]] in 2001.{{cite web|url=http://www.sjuhawks.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jones_dwayne00.html|title=Dwayne Jones|publisher=Saint Joseph's Hawks|access-date=May 12, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222171200/http://www.sjuhawks.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jones_dwayne00.html|archive-date=February 22, 2012}} ==College career== Along with senior [[Jameer Nelson]] and juniors [[Delonte West]] and [[Pat Carroll (basketball)|Pat Carroll]], Jones was an integral part of the undefeated Saint Joseph's team during the 2004 regular season. The Hawks earned a #1 seed in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] and advanced to the [[Elite Eight]]. They were within seconds of the [[Final Four]], before the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]]' [[John Lucas III]] hit a 3-pointer. Saint Joseph's finished with a 30–2 record, the best in the University's history. In 2004–05, Jones was the [[Atlantic 10]] Defensive Player of the Year, and a member of the All-Defensive Team for the second consecutive year. He ranked fifth in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] (11.6) and [[blocked shot|blocks]] (3.0) in the nation, and led the Atlantic 10 in both categories. Jones was named second-team All-Atlantic 10 and All-Big 5, while posting career-best numbers in scoring (10.1 points per game), rebounding and blocked shots. He was also named to the Atlantic 10 All-Championship Team after averaging 10.0 points and 12.7 rebounds in the tournament, and earned [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] All-Tournament honors. Jones' total of 418 rebounds was the second best single-season mark in school history, while his total of 109 blocks was the third best single-season total. He set his career-high with 16 rebounds at [[Old Dominion University|Old Dominion]] and tied it with 16 against [[Hofstra]]. On February 19, 2005, Jones became the first Hawk to notch a triple-double since 1986 with 11 points, 11 rebounds, and career-high 10 blocks against [[St. Bonaventure University|St. Bonaventure]]. ==Professional career== Jones was signed by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on August 26, 2005, as an [[NBA draft|undrafted]] rookie [[free agent]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2143965|title=Wolves sign rookie free agent Dwayne Jones|agency=Associated Press|work=espn.com|date=August 27, 2005}} He was assigned to the [[NBA Development League]]'s [[Florida Flame]] on November 4, 2005. In 26 games for the Flame, Jones averaged 8.9 points, 2.0 blocks (league's third-best, with the total 52 being fifth) and a league leading 11.7 rebounds per game. He also led the league in offensive rebounds per game (4.5), and his 118 total offensive rebounds were good for second place, only eight shy of [[T. J. Cummings]], who played in 22 more games. Without a single official appearance for the Wolves, Jones was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] on January 27, 2006, along with [[Michael Olowokandi]], [[Wally Szczerbiak]] and a future first-round draft choice, in exchange for [[Marcus Banks]], [[Mark Blount]], [[Ricky Davis]], [[Justin Reed]] and two future conditional second-round draft choices. He played in 14 games for the Celtics during [[2005-06 NBA season|the season]], averaging 1.0 points and 2.2 rebounds. Jones had a season high seven points on April 19, 2006 against the [[Miami Heat]] and a career high 13 rebounds on April 17, 2006 against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. Jones was traded to the Cavaliers on October 13, 2006, in exchange for [[Luke Jackson (basketball, born 1981)|Luke Jackson]], and appeared in just 4 regular season games during the [[2006-07 NBA season|2006–2007 season]]. He had three total points (on 3–6 [[free throw]] shooting, against the [[Golden State Warriors]]) and six total rebounds. Jones was assigned by the Cavaliers to the D-League's [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] on March 23, 2007. He played in two games for the Thunderbirds, averaging 11.5 points, 11.5 rebounds, six blocks and two [[steal (basketball)|steals]], including D-League season-high eight blocks on March 24, 2007 against the [[Idaho Stampede]]. In his first full season as an [[NBA]] player, Jones averaged 1 point and 2 rebounds in 56 games during [[2007-08 NBA season|2007–08]], plus 5 [[2008 NBA Playoffs|postseason contests]]. He had a season and career-high nine points and a season-high 12 rebounds on December 4, 2007 against the [[New Jersey Nets]]. In September 2008, Jones was signed by the [[Orlando Magic]] to play in the team's training camp, but was released before [[2008-09 NBA season|the season]] started. He then signed with [[Turkish Basketball League|Turkish League]] club [[Efes Pilsen S.K.]], which also entered the [[Euroleague 2008-09|Euroleague]]. On November 24, 2008, Jones signed with the Charlotte Bobcats.{{cite web | title=Bobcats Sign Dwayne Jones | work=NBA.com | url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/081124_release_jones.html | date=November 24, 2008 | access-date=July 24, 2013 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105034844/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/081124_release_jones.html | archive-date=November 5, 2012 }} On January 8, 2009, Jones was acquired by the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. He was later traded to the [[Idaho Stampede]] for guard Tim Barnes, and then finished the season with the [[Austin Toros]].[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Dwayne-Jones/Summary/255 Dwayne Jones Player Profile – RealGM] On October 17, 2009, Jones signed a one-year contract with Serbian club [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]]. He was signed as their final newcomer for the 2009–10 season.{{cite web | title=Red Star presents Dwayne Jones | work=[[B92]] | date=19 October 2009 |url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2009&mm=10&dd=19&nav_id=387516 | access-date=2009-11-17}} He was released by mutual consent only 5 days after that, due to, as Crvena zvezda general manager said, personal problems that kept him from focusing on professional basketball.{{cite web | title=Red Star released Dwayne Jones | work=[[B92]] | date=21 October 2009 | url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2009&mm=10&dd=21&nav_id=388016 | access-date=2009-11-22}} During those five days in Belgrade, he played in one friendly game versus a minor league team, contributing to the win with 9 points and 5 rebounds. Jones later rejoined the Austin Toros. On April 6, 2010, he was signed by the Phoenix Suns. He was signed to replace Robin Lopez because of a bulging disk and he was the top rebounder in the Development League, averaging 16 rebounds for the Austin Toros. On July 14, 2010 he was traded to the Toronto Raptors along with [[Leandro Barbosa]] in exchange for [[Hedo Türkoğlu]].[http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/barbosa_trade_071410.html Raptors Acquire Barbosa And Jones From Phoenix] However, he was waived by the Raptors on August 13.[http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/jones_waived081310.html Raptors Release Jones] He then re-signed with the Suns on August 30,[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/jones_release_100830.html Suns Sign Dwayne Jones] but he was waived on October 20, 2010.[http://www.azcentral.com/arizonarepublic/sports/articles/2010/10/19/20101019phoenix-suns-golden-state-warriors-preseason.html Phoenix Suns show improvements in preseason win over Golden State Warriors] He also played for [[Fujian SBS Xunxing]] in [[China]] for 2010–11 season.
